question: How do pain points differ by product, segment or region?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Pain points split by product far more than by region: deposit customers complain that their money is stuck, card customers complain that a decision went against them.**

Across checking and savings contacts, 24.9% are about a funds hold or an account restriction; on credit cards the same reason appears in 0.6% of contacts. The card side is the mirror image: rewards and promotions drive 15.0% of card contacts against 2.1% of deposit contacts, and a credit decision or limit dispute is roughly 31 times more likely on a card. These are not two flavours of the same complaint - they need different fixes and different staffing.

The sharpest single deposit pain point is an account closed or frozen that cuts off access to the money: 5.8% of checking and savings contacts against 3.0% of all contacts, a lift of 1.90, and nothing at all on cards, where the comparison puts the upper bound at 0.3%. Read the product detail with care - the by-product breakdown blanks seven of its nine cells, the credit card cell included, because they fall under the minimum support the tool applies, so the small products carry no reportable number either way. The characteristic card failure is a different one: a fraud dispute denied without anyone reviewing the evidence, 12.3% of card contacts against 8.9% overall (lift 1.38), and only 2.6% on money transfer or P2P.

Segment adds exactly one real signal. Older Americans are the group tricked into sending their own money to a scammer: 8.6% of their contacts against 4.8% overall, a lift of 1.79. Servicemembers sit on the average at 4.7%, and the combined older-American-servicemember cell is suppressed for lack of support, so nothing can be said about it. Region is a dead end - the same fraud-dispute theme runs between 7.7% and 10.1% across the five US regions, lifts of 0.87 to 1.13, with confidence intervals that all overlap.

So: route and resource by product, and target scam prevention at older customers. Deposit operations need a funds-release and notice step; card operations need a dispute review that actually looks at the evidence. Building a regional plan would be spending money on noise.

quotes.quote: When I contacted the bank, I was told the investigation could take up to 12 years, which is unreasonable given that the funds are verified wages.
quotes.why: A deposit customer whose verified wages are held with no end date - the deposit-side pain point.

quotes.quote: By freezing my funds for over 30 days, providing conflicting information through over 30 different representatives, and failing to provide a clear legal or factual basis for the freeze, Chase has engaged in practices that are both unfair and abusive to me as a consumer.
quotes.why: The frozen-account pain point in the words of a checking customer.

quotes.quote: But, I guess I authorized a wire transfer! When I realized that I had been scammed I went to my local bank and they had my account locked and flagged.
quotes.why: An older American describing the scam pattern that carries a 1.79 lift for that segment.

quotes.quote: Chase finally told us they viewed the transaction as valid since we had docusigned the contract. Apparently the mere hitting of our Enter key when they read the pages was viewed as a legal signing of a charge we NEVER made.
quotes.why: A second older-American scam case where the bank treated the induced transaction as valid.

caveats: This is a complaint corpus, not a sample of all contacts, so every rate is a share of complaints and not a share of customers.
Complaint dates lag the contact they describe, so the product and segment mix is the mix of who complained, not of who called.
Product, segment and region come from the complaint record, not a customer master; one customer may hold several products.

The breakdown tool blanks any cell with fewer than 50 calls in the slice or fewer than 5 in the theme, so small products (prepaid card, personal loan, student loan) and the combined older-American-servicemember cell carry no reportable number.
followups: Within checking and savings, which specific hold reasons drive the funds-release backlog, and how long do they last?
Are older Americans more often scammed, or equally scammed and less often reimbursed?

SELECT c.month, COUNT(*) AS n_calls, ROUND(SUM(1.0 / c.sampling_fraction)) AS population_estimate FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY c.month ORDER BY c.month

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY n_calls DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
SELECT tc.theme_id, tc.call_id FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND tc.theme_id IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ORDER BY c.date DESC, tc.call_id
SELECT e.overall_sentiment AS v, COUNT(*) AS n FROM extractions e JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY v ORDER BY n DESC, v
SELECT e.resolution_status AS v, COUNT(*) AS n FROM extractions e JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY v ORDER BY n DESC, v
SELECT e.customer_ask AS v, COUNT(*) AS n FROM extractions e JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY v ORDER BY n DESC, v
